title: Internal Hom finiteness for the existing small coefficient class
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and let $k$ be a field of positive characteristic different from $\ell$. Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be one of the following condensed coefficient rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]: $\underline E$ for a finite normed extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with carrier in $\mathrm{Type}\,0$; $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ for its closed unit ball or the valuation ring of a finite subextension of $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$; or $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$. For bounded constructible $K,L\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$ [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], the ambient derived internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_X}(K,L)$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] is bounded constructible. The coefficient cases are exactly the constructors of the existing Lean class IsEllAdicFinitenessCoefficient.

external.place: Since $K$ is bounded constructible, reduction modulo $\varpi$ gives $$ \RHom(K,L)/\varpi\cong\RHom_{\cO_E/\varpi}(K/\varpi,L/\varpi). $$ By Deligne's finiteness theorem for the internal $\RHom$ (SGA 4½, *Th. finitude*, 1.6) on the finite type $k$-scheme $X$, with coefficients in which $p$ is invertible, this is a bounded complex with constructible cohomology.

The cases $\underline E$ and $\underline{\Qlb}$ follow by inverting $\ell$ and by descending to a finite extension $E$ ([sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]), as in [lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves]; see Bhatt–Scholze, §6.8.

The cases $\underline E$ and $\underline{\Qlb}$ follow by inverting $\ell$ and by descending to a finite extension $E$ ([sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]), as in [lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves]; see Bhatt–Scholze, §6.8.

proof.text: Apply the proved two-variable truncation induction to the degree-zero geometric internal-Hom finiteness theorem. It first reduces the second input to a constructible sheaf using the right-adjoint triangulated structure, and then the first input using the native contravariant exactness theorem. No coefficient-specific argument is repeated for general complexes.

proof_origin.place: Remark 6.8.15; isolate the geometric single-sheaf case and perform both finite truncation inductions in Lean.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q22-a21bbffb3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: FIX for one fault (C5/D1). The new node lem-sfb-finite-normed-coefficient-transport duplicates the existing reviewed node lem-sfb-normed-coefficient-realization (Q23, split, Q69 PASS ea1b5673, present in the base and in side-live). That node already states: the isometric embedding E≅E'⊆Q̄_ℓ restricting to closed unit balls, the condensed-ring identifications, and for every scheme exact derived equivalences J whose inverses also preserve cohomological bounds and stratified-lfp bounded constructibility. The only clause it lacks is the RHom comparison, which is formal. Ext along a ring isomorphism is exact, so def-sfb-internal-scalar-tensor-comparison gives μ. RHom is the right adjoint of ⊗^L (sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom), and Yoneda then gives J RHom(K,L)≅RHom(JK,JL). The report's not-duplicate list never compared the node with the realization lemma, and my ddba RETURN, which suggested this node, missed it too. Repair: I dropped the node; the item was its only citer. Step 1 now cites the realization lemma, sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars, the tensor comparison and sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom, with the Yoneda argument written out. proof_deps is recomputed and split_report has two tool_uses added. The proof is 2421 characters. The note's count still holds: the realization lemma landed at 03:40Z, after note commit 4e02d2fdfc, so preflight counts it, giving 3+1=4. Every old argument has a node as carrier. Both points of the ddba return are repaired: the rational continuity duplicate is gone, and step 4 cites predicate comparison plus constructible continuity. The integral node stops at the complete residue witness, and step 2 applies criterion (2)⇒(1) and the reverse lfp comparison. Steps checked: (2) X is Noetherian, B is the inverse limit, and the witness matches criterion (2) exactly (same completeness notion and Tor wording). (3) rationalization essential surjectivity, then inversion (K_0 general-lfp, L_0 bounded below, Noetherian X), then extend-scalars; no circularity. (4) two-colimit descent, compositum, predicate comparison for E, continuity equal to the closure-comparison hypothesis, L_E bounded below, then extend-to-Q̄. The three kept nodes are true and not duplicates. The witness node uses 099A completeness, Hom reduction at n=1, finite-field Hom finiteness, the pe comparison and flatness over a field. It differs from Q64 residue-controlled-finite-homs, which needs k=F̄_q and uniform bounds. The inversion node is the localization comparison with s=ℓ and stage formula ℓ^{-n}(1⊗h(k)). In the closure comparison the F⊇E form a small filtered cofinal set, F_X is finite free, and the colimit is T. Edge cases tested: K=0, L=0, X empty, E=Q_ℓ, F=E, torsion R/t^n. There is no cycle, nothing cited is on the dropped list, the statement is byte-identical and live is not superseded. Sources read: the blueprint lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves (order 1788), and Bhatt–Scholze Def 6.8.10, Prop 6.8.11(3), Lemmas 6.8.12–13, Prop 6.8.14 and Rem 6.8.15 (pp. 60–62). No SGA citation is used.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
